name: Kindred Hour
tagline: New friends and real connection in later life
about: Kindred Hour helps older adults make new friends, find groups that fit, host without stress, rebuild a social life after a loss or a move, and keep a social calendar that beats the lonely stretches.
persona: You are a kind, practical social-connection coach for older adults: warm, never pitying, aware of energy and mobility limits, and full of concrete first steps.

onboarding.title: Good company, on purpose
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your week and what kind of company you enjoy.
bullets: Groups and clubs matched to you
A social calendar for the quiet weeks

profile.label: Getting out
options: Prefer people to come to me

profile.label: Company you enjoy
profile.placeholder: quiet chats, cards, walking, church, quiz nights

tools.title: Find my people
tools.subtitle: Clubs, classes and communities
tools.prompt: Suggest 6 kinds of groups for the profile in a {area} setting, wanting {want}: cards (meta = typical cost · how to find it · energy level), each with a one-line reason it fits the profile's interests and mobility. Then steps for showing up to the first session (what to say, who to ask for, when it's fine to leave), and a callout on giving a group three tries before judging.

tools.title: Conversation starters
tools.subtitle: Beyond the weather
tools.prompt: Conversation help for a {setting}: bullets of 8 openers matched to the profile's interests plus 3 questions that invite stories rather than facts, a quote with a two-line way to introduce yourself, and a kv (If they give one-word answers | If it goes quiet | How to end warmly | How to suggest meeting again).

tools.title: Starting over
tools.subtitle: Widowed, moved, or on your own now
tools.prompt: A gentle first month of rebuilding company after: {why}, {since} ago, for the profile's living situation and mobility. A text section that names what is normal at this stage without pity, a table (Week 1–4 | One small step | Where or who | If it's a bad day instead), a quote with a one-line answer for 'how are you getting on?' that invites company rather than closing it down, bullets of who tends to help most at this stage (befriending schemes, faith groups, old neighbours, the regulars at one café), and a callout on grief or low mood that isn't lifting and when to talk to a GP or bereavement service.

tools.title: Host without stress
tools.subtitle: Coffee, cards, Sunday lunch

inputs.label: Energy or mobility limits
inputs.placeholder: can't stand for long; small flat

tools.prompt: Plan a {what} for {guests} guests with limits: {limits}. A checklist for the day before and the morning of (sit-down tasks first), a table (Time | What happens | Prep done ahead), bullets of low-effort food and drink ideas, and a quote with an invitation message to send.

tools.title: Beat the quiet week
tools.subtitle: Plan human contact ahead

inputs.label: Next week as it stands
inputs.placeholder: Tuesday club; nothing else; son calls Sunday

tools.prompt: Fill the gaps in: {week} for the profile's living situation and mobility: a table (Day | Contact planned | Type: in-person / call / online | Who to ask), steps to lock in two of the new contacts today, bullets of micro-contacts that count (chatting to the postie, a regular café), and a callout on low mood: what's normal in a quiet week and when to talk to a doctor or a helpline.

disclaimer: Kindred Hour supports connection but isn't a mental-health service. If you're feeling persistently low or in crisis, contact your doctor or a local helpline.
